title: Opportunities and Pipelines
learningGoal: Learn how to use Opportunities and Pipelines to track leads, monitor sales status, and keep follow-up clear.

items.title: Leads Slip Through the Cracks
items.description: Most leads are not lost because the person said no. They're lost because you didn't follow up at the right time or forgot the next step.

items.title: Inbox vs Pipeline
items.description: The inbox shows the conversation. The pipeline shows the business status. You need both to manage leads effectively.

items.title: The Solution
items.description: LeadProspectrr separates conversations from opportunities, giving you a clear visual board to track where each lead stands.

items.title: A Potential Client
items.description: An Opportunity is a lead or contact that could become a client or customer. Someone who has shown interest in working with you.

items.title: Examples of Opportunities
items.description: Someone fills out a form, books a call, asks for pricing, replies to your text or email, or asks about working together.

items.title: Don't Let Them Sit
items.description: These people should not just sit in the inbox. They should be tracked as Opportunities with clear next steps.

items.title: A Visual Board
items.description: A Pipeline is a visual board that shows where each lead stands in your sales process at a glance.

items.title: The Bucket Analogy
items.description: Think of a pipeline like a row of buckets. Each lead sits in the bucket that matches where they are right now.

items.title: Know What to Do
items.description: The pipeline helps you know who needs a reply, who needs a proposal, and who may be ready to buy.

items.title: New Lead
items.description: Interest shown, but no action taken yet. This is where all fresh opportunities start.

items.title: Contacted
items.description: You have replied or reached out to the lead. The conversation has begun.

items.title: Appointment Booked
items.description: The lead has scheduled a call or consultation. A meeting is on the calendar.

items.title: Proposal Sent
items.description: Pricing or proposal has been delivered. Waiting for the lead to review and respond.

items.title: Won
items.description: The lead has agreed to move forward. They are now a client or customer.

items.title: Lost
items.description: Not moving forward at this time. This is not a failure—just a closed opportunity.

keyPoint: The golden rule of pipeline management: Never leave a lead without a clear next action. Every opportunity should have a stage and a defined follow-up step.

actionSteps.title: Open the Opportunities Area
actionSteps.description: Navigate to Opportunities in LeadProspectrr and review your current pipeline stages.

actionSteps.title: Create a Sample Opportunity
actionSteps.description: Add a test opportunity with a name, estimated value, and place it in the New Lead stage.

actionSteps.title: Practice Moving Stages
actionSteps.description: Move your test opportunity through each pipeline stage and add notes at each step.

actionSteps.title: Set a Daily Reminder
actionSteps.description: Schedule 5 minutes each day to check your pipeline and update lead stages.

quizzes.question: What is the main difference between the inbox and the pipeline?

options.option_text: The inbox is faster than the pipeline
The inbox shows conversations, the pipeline shows business status

quizzes.explanation: The inbox shows what the person said (conversations), while the pipeline shows where they stand in your sales process (business status). You need both to manage leads effectively.

quizzes.question: Which of these is NOT a standard pipeline stage?
quizzes.explanation: Standard pipeline stages are: New Lead, Contacted, Appointment Booked, Proposal Sent, Won, and Lost. 'Waiting Forever' is not a valid stage—leads should always have clear next actions.

quizzes.question: What is the golden rule of pipeline management?

options.option_text: Never leave a lead without a clear next action
Move leads to Won as quickly as possible
Check the pipeline once per month

quizzes.explanation: The golden rule is to never leave a lead without a clear next action. Every opportunity should have a defined stage and a specific follow-up step to prevent leads from falling through the cracks.
